comparison: Both evaluate activity assay data (C43-C46) showing ATP activation and dATP inhibition. OpenEval finds the kinetic characterization well-supported with clear parameters. Peer reviewers describe the biochemical experiments as 'solid' and do not question the activity data, indicating agreement on the validity of these measurements.

Both address nucleotide binding data from ITC and MST (C47-C54). OpenEval finds the data consistent and acknowledges the ITC/MST discrepancy as explained. Peer reviewers note 'some open questions remain about the interpretation of activity/binding assays,' suggesting uncertainty about interpretation despite accepting the binding experiments as part of complementary characterization.

Both evaluate oligomerization shifts (C55-C56). OpenEval supports the GEMMA data showing nucleotide-dependent oligomeric changes but notes uncertainty about functional significance. Peer reviewers describe 'striking differences in oligomerization' as an established finding, treating the oligomerization shift as validated without expressing the same reservations about functional interpretation.

Both address EPR data on glycyl radical formation (C57-C59, C10). OpenEval finds the observation that radicals form even with dATP to be critical and well-documented. Peer reviewers acknowledge EPR as part of complementary biochemical characterization without raising concerns, indicating agreement on the validity of this counterintuitive finding.

Both evaluate substrate binding measurements (C60-C63, C11). OpenEval strongly supports the MST data showing >100-fold affinity difference and finds the mechanistic conclusion well-justified. Peer reviewers note 'some open questions remain about the interpretation of activity/binding assays,' suggesting the mechanistic interpretation may require clarification despite the data being part of accepted characterization.

Both evaluate domain architecture and structural features from cryo-EM (C64-C71 and overlapping claims C72-C91). OpenEval finds structural assignments well-supported and identifies the NxN flap as novel. Peer reviewers describe the cryo-EM characterization as 'solid' and 'impressive, in-depth structural analysis,' indicating strong agreement on the quality and validity of the structural data.

OpenEval evaluates ATP-CTP structure features (C73-C79) as well-supported, noting asymmetry and novel ATP-cone orientation. Peer reviewers' assessment of 'solid' cryo-EM characterization encompasses these structural details, though they group them with broader structural analysis rather than evaluating separately.

OpenEval evaluates active site architecture (C80-C85) as well-supported by electron density and consistent with formate-dependent mechanism. Peer reviewers' 'solid' cryo-EM assessment includes these structural details as part of the comprehensive structural characterization.

OpenEval evaluates NxN flap structural observations (C86-C90) as well-supported by cryo-EM data. Peer reviewers include this in their 'impressive, in-depth structural analysis' and specifically highlight the flap's ordering/disordering as a principal finding, indicating strong agreement on this novel structural element.

OpenEval evaluates substrate tunnel analysis (C91-C92) as supported by computational analysis, noting speculation about functional significance. Peer reviewers' broad assessment of structural characterization as 'solid' may encompass this, though they do not specifically comment on the tunnel analysis.

Both evaluate ATP-dTTP-GTP structure showing half-of-sites activity (C93-C99). OpenEval finds the asymmetry and differential loop conformations clearly demonstrated and mechanistically important. Peer reviewers acknowledge this as part of 'striking differences in oligomerization and (dis)ordering of select structural features,' indicating agreement on the structural observations.

Both evaluate dATP-bound dimer showing disorder (C100-C104, C9). OpenEval finds the GRD disorder clearly demonstrated and well-supported by comparison with ATP structures. Peer reviewers specifically identify 'the disordering (or increased protein dynamics) of both this flap and the glycyl radical domain (GRD)' as a principal finding, indicating strong agreement.

Both evaluate dATP-bound tetramer structure (C105-C114). OpenEval finds the novel oligomeric arrangement well-documented but questions functional significance due to small buried surface area. Peer reviewers note 'striking differences in oligomerization' without questioning the structure itself, implicitly accepting it as part of solid cryo-EM characterization while functional significance remains less clear.

Both evaluate dATP-CTP complexes showing no bound substrate (C115-C116). OpenEval finds this strong evidence that dATP prevents substrate binding and supports the mechanism. Peer reviewers note the correlation between dATP binding and 'loss of substrate binding' as a key finding, indicating agreement though interpretation questions may remain.

Both evaluate HDX-MS data (C117-C122). OpenEval finds the data supports structural findings and the trend toward increased dynamics with dATP supports the mechanism, while noting limitations. Peer reviewers note 'some open questions remain about the interpretation of...the HDX-MS results,' acknowledging it complements cryo-EM but requires clarification, indicating partial agreement with interpretation uncertainty.

Both evaluate the main mechanistic conclusion (C123-C125, C8, C12, C41). OpenEval finds the mechanism well-supported by combined data though molecular details remain incomplete. Peer reviewers identify this as 'one of the principal findings' providing 'new insights/views into the subtle differences of nucleotide modulation,' indicating strong agreement on the core mechanistic discovery.

OpenEval evaluates main findings summary (C6-C12) as supported and representing core discovery. Peer reviewers' assessment overlaps partially with oligomerization findings (C6-C7 in R3) and mechanistic conclusions (C8, C12 in R12), treating these as validated principal findings across multiple review points.

OpenEval's summary of main findings (C6-C12) overlaps with peer reviewers' assessment of the mechanistic conclusion (C8, C12). Both agree this represents a major discovery showing a fundamentally different inhibition mechanism, with peer reviewers highlighting it as providing 'new insights/views' into RNR allostery.

Both evaluate comparative conclusions about class I vs III mechanisms (C39-C41). OpenEval finds the comparison well-established and the class III mechanism a major conceptual advance. Peer reviewers explicitly state the work provides 'evidence for new insights/views into the subtle differences' and note the mechanism differs from class I, indicating strong agreement on this comparative contribution.

Both evaluate detailed class I/III mechanistic comparisons (C126-C130). OpenEval finds the comparison provides important evolutionary and mechanistic context. Peer reviewers treat this comparative analysis as valuable for understanding RNR allostery and central to the 'new insights/views into the subtle differences of nucleotide modulation,' indicating agreement on the value of this comparison.

OpenEval evaluates background knowledge and knowledge gap (C1-C5, C13-C38) as well-supported by literature and appropriately motivating the study. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers focus on experimental findings rather than background claims.

OpenEval evaluates DALI server structural comparison analysis (C72) as supported and providing appropriate context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though this structural comparison may be implicitly included in peer reviewers' assessment of solid structural characterization (R6).
